reachable: Yes, and I checked this specifically at the scored position rather than assuming it. Scoring layout is [cmd_0,obs_0,...,cmd_r] with rpos = 2*r (cups_probe.build_cups_layout), so the read is a COMMAND position and the module's contribution is added exactly there (`pred[:, 0::2] += contrib`, gated only by valid_cmd, which is True at the read). On a cups-shaped batch the r24-minus-r22 delta at rpos is nonzero for both a full row (0.0186) and a shorter padded row (0.0256), while the delta at every observation position is exactly 0.0. The "gated on an observation being present" failure mode does NOT bite here: obs_live is indeed False at the read (measured: absorb=0 at the read), but absorb at position i is only ever used as an ABSORPTION TARGET for chases starting at strictly later positions — the chase starting AT the read uses follow[read, j<read] and absorb at earlier steps, all of which are live. Causality holds: perturbing the observation at pair j by 3-sigma moves the command prediction at every index <= j by exactly 0.0 and moves later ones by 0.9-3.0. Gradient: all 19 new parameters receive nonzero gradient at STEP 1 under the genome's own objective (r12_antiretrieval_ring_negatives), head (r2_dualaddress_move_transport) and optim (r18 Muon + spectral cap); six real steps give finite, decreasing losses. The 0.05*I readout does buy first-order gradient to the addressing from step 1, as claimed. Caveat worth carrying: the addressing gradients are small in absolute terms (role_src 1.5e-6, addr_proj 4.3e-5) versus the gate (4.4e-3), so the author's own stated risk #2 — the chase learning too slowly for the step budget — is the live one. AdamW second-moment normalization mitigates it; global clip_grad_norm 1.0 does not. chase_out.weight is (768,768) so it IS captured by the optim's spectral cap, as claimed; addr_proj.weight (64,256) is a shape singleton and so goes to AdamW, not Muon — the hypothesis does not claim otherwise.
solves_outside_model: No. The claim "No command text is parsed anywhere; nothing in this file knows what 'mv' is" is literally true — the module contains no string operations at all, never touches `batch["cmds"]` or step metadata, and consumes only tok_emb/types/key_pad. Nothing resolved is written back into the model's INPUT: the chase result is added to `pred` at command positions, downstream of the trunk. The retracted-stream shape (resolving the chain in Python and stamping the answer into the read token) is structurally absent. The genome's head (r2_dualaddress_move_transport) also mines its aux examples by embedding duplication, not by parsing commands. I verified the chase algebra with an oracle-addressed forward pass on a 3-move chain (cat A, cat X, mv A B, mv B C, mv C E, read cat E): the recovered copy has cosine 1.0000 with A's content and -0.064 with X's; re-pointing the first hop at the partner (the role-swap) flips it to cosine 1.0000 with X's content. That reproduces the author's claim exactly, and it is the honest kind of verification — it shows the arithmetic composes given correct addresses, and says nothing about whether the frozen encoder yields those addresses. The data premise also checks out: mv observations render to the constant "cwd=/ exit=0\n" (render_obs at realenv/seq_worldmodel.py:38) so a move step carries no content and must be a pass-through node, and the cups_test `cat <final path>` observation is byte-identical to its exposure `cat <original path>` observation, so a correct chase yields a vector that is literally in the forced-foil candidate bank.
summary: The code implements what the hypothesis describes. Every structural claim replicates: one shared GELU feature layer, two learned diagonal sigmoid role gates, ONE shared addr_proj R^256 -> R^64 with unit-normalized outputs; follow[j,j'] = softmax over strictly-earlier valid commands of <src_j, dst_j'>/temp minus softplus(recency)*(j-j'-1); absorb = sigmoid(MLP(a, obs_feat)) * obs_live; the K-hop recursion alpha_{t+1} = (alpha_t*(1-absorb)) @ follow with acc = sum_t alpha_t*absorb, K=8 hops (loop runs chase_hops-1 = 7 extra times, giving alpha_1..alpha_8); copy = acc @ obs / max(mass,1e-4); chase_out initialized to EXACTLY 0.05*I with zero bias; softplus(recency) init 0.2519 ("~0.25" as claimed); temp init 0.5 with unit-norm addresses giving the claimed +/-2 score range; absorb 0.500-0.509 at every live step at init, so all hops do carry mass. acc mass is a proper sub-probability (max row sum 0.764 at init, spread over four earlier steps). The genome is exactly the parent's with only the arch axis changed, subclassing r22 so both the r18 trunk and the r22 prefix-copy channel survive, and keeping the parent's r2 head while dropping the partner's — as stated. Robustness claims hold: finite correct-shape outputs for L in {0,1,2,3,4,5,7,33}, padded rows, fully-padded rows and the odd-L read layout. What I could NOT check: (a) whether the frozen encoder's mean-pooled `mv A B` embedding actually separates the two paths, and whether a `cat P` command lands P at the same dst address a later `mv P Q` puts at its src address — this is the whole bet and needs the encoder plus the embedding cache, neither of which is present locally; (b) whether 8 hops of end-to-end chase learn inside the step budget given the 1e-6..1e-5 addressing gradients; (c) whether the recency prior collapses the chase into a fixed-position lookup, which would land it in the analytic band the run reports rather than in genuine tracking — the author names this failure mode himself. All "CORRECTNESS CHECKED HERE" numbers were written without ever running torch; I re-ran them and every substantive one replicates (init delta, exact-zero causality, shape sweep, six finite training steps, gradient to all new params, oracle chase cosine 1.000 with the role-swap flip), with only the +8% timing figure landing off at +2.7% here.

divergences.claim: "...injected into pred at command position i through a (D,D) readout initialized to 0.05*I ... under a sigmoid gate fed the absorbed mass, the chase sharpness and the copy's RMS" (hypothesis §4, and the module DESCRIPTION: "under a sigmoid gate fed the absorbed mass and the chase sharpness").
divergences.what_the_code_does: chase_gate = nn.Linear(self.d + 3, 1) and is fed torch.cat([h_out[:, 0::2, :], feat]) — the FULL trunk hidden state at that command position, plus the three scalars. The gate is therefore context-conditioned by the whole causal trunk, not only by the three chase statistics the hypothesis names. This is the same shape as r22's x_gate, it is causal, and it does not create leakage; it just makes the gate a richer function than described.

divergences.what_the_code_does: Re-measured on this machine (torch 2.13, 4 threads, median of 9 alternating fwd+bwd at B=64, L=64): r22 565.0 ms, r24 580.3 ms → +2.7%. Direction and order of magnitude are right; the specific figure is not reproducible here, and could not have been produced by the author (no torch in the jail).

divergences.claim: "forward is bit-comparable to r22 at init up to the 0.05*I readout (max |delta| 0.028)."
divergences.what_the_code_does: True in substance, number is input-dependent. On a cups-shaped batch (odd L=9, one padded row) max |delta| = 0.019 and 0.026 per row — consistent with 0.028. On unit-normal tokens it is 0.047. Inherited parameters are bit-identical to r22 under the same manual_seed (new modules are constructed after super().__init__, preserving the init-RNG stream), and the delta is exactly 0.0 at every observation position.
divergences.evidence: Same-seed build of r22 and r24: all 3,687,992 inherited parameters compare equal; 886,199 new parameters. Delta at obs positions max 0.0; delta confined to command positions.

divergences.claim: "WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE FOR IT TO FAIL — The pooled frozen embedding of 'mv A B' may not linearly separate A from B ... This is the single biggest risk."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The risk is real but stated narrowly. The chase's terminal hop must match the FIRST mv's src_addr against the exposure step's dst_addr, and the exposure step is `cat /tmp/w/cups/...` — a different command type, different token neighbourhood, different pooling. So the design also requires two different command kinds to land the same path string at the same 64-d address, which is a harder ask than separating the two paths inside one mv. The hypothesis does not name this half.
divergences.evidence: evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl: exposures are `cat <path>`, moves are `mv <src> <dst>`, read is `cat <final path>`. The chase from the read must traverse mv→mv→mv→cat.
